newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian journalists unhappy with media freedom.
newsitem.headline: Croatian journalists unhappy with media freedom.

text.p: Most Croatian journalists are unhappy with the freedom of the media in their country and say they need a great deal of courage to be independent under political pressure, an independent poll showed on Wednesday.

"Journalists are dissatisfied with the stagnation or even degradation of media freedom since the first multi-party elections (in 1990)," the media and market research agency Pulse said in a press release.

The survey, carried out in April on 415 journalists from both state-run and independent media, showed some 72.5 percent described various political pressures as the biggest problem for Croatian journalists.
Some 65 percent thought the media were not free enough and 88.3 percent said journalists needed courage to stay professionally independent.
The majority of 21.7 percent of those happy with media freedom are members of the ruling Croatian Democratic Party (HDZ), older than 50, religious and have lower education.
Also, 48.1 percent of journalists believe domestic political editors have more of a political than a journalistic role, the poll showed.

Jagoda Vukusic, head of the Croatian Journalists' Association which ordered the survey, told reporters on Wednesday the first poll of its kind to be conducted in Croatia reflected the mood of journalists in the country.
"Dissatisfaction does not change with their job status. Editors and commentators are equally unhappy with media freedom as their younger colleagues or freelancers," the Pulse release said.
Nenad Bulat, a Pulse employee, told a news conference: "Only 23.7 percent think that the media are more free today than they were in 1989, which is a disastrous result."
The Croatian government has been criticised for its firm hold over the media and treatment of independent journalists.
The state has a monopoly over three main dailies, the television and the national radio, which are perceived as government mouthpieces.
Journalists working for satirical opposition weekly Feral Tribune have been continually fined for insulting high state officials.
